items.resolution: With no allowlisted schemas, show the named configuration-empty guidance and no action targeting an implicit schema.
items.probe: What is shown when there is no data — zero items, an unfilled form, or absent media?

items.resolution: While queue/backend observation runs, retain the last complete observed values with their snapshot and expose a named busy refresh control.
items.probe: What is shown while data or content is still loading (skeleton, spinner, progressive reveal)?

items.resolution: A failed queue/backend observation names its unavailable source and reason, retains known evidence, and offers refresh without claiming a remote operation failed.
items.probe: What is shown when the load or submit fails (message, retry affordance, partial fallback)?

items.resolution: For a selected schema, show queue and backend observations under separate labels with full schema and index identity; do not roll them into contract or document success.
items.probe: What does the normal populated (happy-path) state look like at a typical volume of content?

items.resolution: When only one observation source is available, keep that known result and identify the other source as unavailable instead of substituting zero or healthy.
items.probe: What is shown for partial or incomplete data — some fields or rows present, others missing?

items.resolution: Schema modules and index names wrap or reflow within the existing selector/result layout; essential identity is not clipped and the page does not gain horizontal overflow.
items.probe: What happens when content exceeds its container — scroll, clip, wrap, or truncate?

items.resolution: No configured schema uses the empty guidance; one or many configured schemas keep an explicit selected target and never silently switch actions to a different schema.
items.probe: How does the layout read at zero, one, and many items (singular vs plural copy, spacing)?

items.resolution: Long schema modules, index names, and observation reasons remain readable at narrow widths and are not available only through a tooltip.
items.probe: What happens with unusually long text — truncation, wrapping, ellipsis, or reflow?

items.resolution: Before contract or document checks run, identify each result as not checked; no empty result is presented as a matching contract or present document.
items.probe: What is shown when there is no data — zero items, an unfilled form, or absent media?

items.resolution: During either check, name the in-flight observation and leave the independent contract/document result visible without changing it to success.
items.probe: What is shown while data or content is still loading (skeleton, spinner, progressive reveal)?

items.resolution: A contract-check or document-observation failure identifies which check could not be checked, retains its reason, and remains unknown rather than a remote task failure.
items.probe: What is shown when the load or submit fails (message, retry affordance, partial fallback)?

items.resolution: Show declared-versus-live contract findings and expected-document presence as independent results with their applicable index/document evidence.
items.probe: What does the normal populated (happy-path) state look like at a typical volume of content?

items.resolution: If contract evidence is complete but document evidence is unavailable (or vice versa), retain the known result and explicitly label the other one incomplete; one cannot stand in for the other.
items.probe: What is shown for partial or incomplete data — some fields or rows present, others missing?

items.resolution: Long field names, index names, document identifiers, and mismatch reasons wrap within the named evidence region without hiding row labels or causing page-level horizontal scroll.
items.probe: What happens when content exceeds its container — scroll, clip, wrap, or truncate?

items.resolution: Zero mismatches and multiple mismatch rows use explicit counts and the same result structure; zero contract drift never implies that expected documents are present.
items.probe: How does the layout read at zero, one, and many items (singular vs plural copy, spacing)?

items.resolution: Full field/document/index identifiers and mismatch reasons remain selectable and readable without truncating the only evidence.
items.probe: What happens with unusually long text — truncation, wrapping, ellipsis, or reflow?
